official_title: Sequential Collision-Aware Kinematic Control of Robot Manipulators Using Control Barrier Functions and Learned Link Selection
semantic_distinctions: Use task for a controller objective; distinguish it from the physical manipulation operation
Joint configuration q and spatial pose (p,R) remain distinct
Direct does not mean a straight Cartesian path
Use episode for dataset cases; preserve historical source identifiers and filenames
Spatial Manipulator is the presentation label for the Franka Emika model; archived paths and source identifiers remain unchanged
The common control framework changes model-specific IK, task-error/CLF, and geometric CBF components
Goncalves basic circulation theory assumes even configuration dimension; its separate odd-dimensional extension is not excluded
Train-best fixed pair (3,5) is selected by highest training success and held unchanged on Validation/Test
Full task sequence mathcal S includes the final EE task; candidate pair S_k contains only two link subtasks from Omega
Spatial mathcal S_all denotes seven link subtasks followed by a final EE subtask
Generic CLF background uses c_V; the updated method uses link-specific c_i
Planar plotted CLFs use the current thesis normalization on archived trajectories; this is not a new controller experiment
Abstract learning context uses R_d; its numerical encoder input uses a six-dimensional representation
10-pair mean is the expected outcome of uniform candidate-pair choice; paired time comparisons condition the uniform episode-pair distribution on joint success with the comparison method
Main results compare Learned selection against the 10-pair mean; the Train-best fixed pair is a separate stronger reference in Appendix A14.
Example pair (3,5) denotes one stored trajectory in the single-episode illustration, never an average trajectory.
Uncertainty for the 10-pair mean uses paired resampling of complete episodes, not independent resampling of episode-pair records.
A subtask is a regulation objective; a subtask target is its desired position or pose. Link subtasks precede the final EE subtask.
Use subgoals for the human-reaching literature; these are not the robot controller's formal link subtasks.
3.2.1 uses the user-requested display title Decomposition of Regulation Task; the thesis source title is recorded separately until renamed.
The literal 3.3.2 thesis heading Intermediate Position Tasks and Final Pose Task remains as a chapter reference.
Common obstacle encoder means the same parameterized encoder is applied to every obstacle.
Identical CLF form refers to the mathematical structure, not identical functions, parameter values or evaluated CLF values.
Success in both means both compared methods succeed; preserve the distinction between episodes and episode-pair outcomes.
